analysis:
The PR is a documentation-only change to docs/provider/cli-reference.md. It adds one row at head line 1751 to the LaunchAgent environment passthrough table: `DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES`, read by `DeadlineAdmissionFixes.environmentKey` in AdmissionRateEstimators.swift. The row sits among the other scheduler and admission tunables (e.g. `DARKBLOOM_PREFILL_DEADLINE_MODE`) that `darkbloom start` copies from the invoking shell into the provider plist. I read all three base units (831-1806) and the patch. No authorization, attestation, encryption or coordinator wire behavior is documented as changing.

The row implies a new daemon-forwarded env key (`LaunchAgent.passthroughEnvKeys`/`inferencePassthroughEnvKeys`) that influences deadline/TTFT admission. The Swift implementation and LaunchAgent.swift are not in the supplied evidence, so I cannot confirm that the doc matches the code. The key is a local operator-controlled scheduling tunable, and the operator already has full control of the local provider config under TB-003. I see no plausible exposure of A-001 (prompts), A-003 or the attestation assets, and no concrete regression.

Related threat context is T-041, the prefix-cache TTFT timing oracle. The patch does not touch prefix-cache gating, TTL, HMAC lookup or salt scoping, so the T-041 mitigations are unaffected. Unverified contracts for the next pass: (1) that the key is actually added to the passthrough list in LaunchAgent.swift; (2) that the TTFT admission change cannot affect availability (T-010, T-029) or leak per-tenant timing. These are code questions outside this docs-only diff and do not support a finding here.
